strange-things-are-afoot-talking-to-goss.speaker: Gossip
strange-things-are-afoot-talking-to-goss.text: Oh, I remember you. You're the one that discovered Lord Sinclair's murderer. Well, I can tell you, strange things are afoot once again.

strange-things-are-afoot-talking-to-goss.speaker: Gossip
strange-things-are-afoot-talking-to-goss.text: Well, you didn't hear it from me, but I've heard the Sinclair family have vamoosed! Just up and left the mansion.

strange-things-are-afoot-talking-to-goss.player: You mean they let the murderer get away?

strange-things-are-afoot-talking-to-goss.speaker: Gossip
strange-things-are-afoot-talking-to-goss.text: Of course not! Anna's safely locked in the Seers' Village jail. She'll be going to trial soon, so I've heard.

strange-things-are-afoot-talking-to-goss.player: Anna? Is that who they arrested? I thought...hmm, never mind.

strange-things-are-afoot-talking-to-goss.speaker: Gossip
strange-things-are-afoot-talking-to-goss.text: Yes, the guards received evidence from one of the family members that conclusively proved Anna did it. All other evidence was thrown out, it was that good.

strange-things-are-afoot-talking-to-goss.speaker: Gossip
strange-things-are-afoot-talking-to-goss.text: So they arrested her and soon the case will go to court.

strange-things-are-afoot-talking-to-goss.player: So, why is it a big deal that the Sinclairs have left, then? Maybe they wanted to get away from the memory of their father's death.

strange-things-are-afoot-talking-to-goss.speaker: Gossip
strange-things-are-afoot-talking-to-goss.text: Well, it wouldn't be suspicious at all, but King Arthur has also disappeared.

strange-things-are-afoot-talking-to-goss.speaker: Gossip
strange-things-are-afoot-talking-to-goss.text: No one has seen him or the knights in quite a while. Quite a coincidence, don't you think?

steps.player: How curious. Maybe I should investigate it.

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: You didn't hear it from me, but I believe that guard in the garden is also investigating it. He might be able to tell you more.

steps.player: Very odd coincidence, but I don't really have time to look into it now.

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: Ah, too bad. I'll have to get news from my other sources.

strange-things-are-afoot-talking-to-goss.speaker: Gossip
strange-things-are-afoot-talking-to-goss.text: Have you spoken to the guard by the mansion? He won't tell me much, he called me a gossip - the nerve - but he might be willing to speak to you.

peril-at-the-end-house-trying-to-open-th.text: You can't open the door, it's locked tight.

peril-at-the-end-house-investigating-the.text: A slightly broken window. Could be easily shattered.

peril-at-the-end-house-trying-to-break-i.text: You need the guards' permission to do that.

peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-pierre.player: You know, this has been bugging me for a while: Why do the Sinclairs have a dog handler on the payroll when they only have one dog?

peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-pierre.speaker: Pierre
peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-pierre.text: Have you seen that dog? It's a nasty piece of work. Even I don't like going near it.

peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-stanfo.speaker: Stanford
peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-stanfo.text: 'Allo. I don't think you'll be able to visit the mansion today, it's been locked up tight for a while now.

peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-the-gu.speaker: Guard
peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-the-gu.text: Good day, [player name]. I'm afraid we meet under strange circumstances again.

peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-the-gu.player: So I have heard. The town gossip informed me that something was amiss. I've come to offer my assistance.

peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-the-gu.speaker: Guard
peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-the-gu.text: Finally, that man serves a purpose. I'm glad to have your help. I'm baffled again and my hands are tied.

peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-the-gu.speaker: Guard
peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-the-gu.text: The Sinclairs have disappeared, though I'm not sorry to see them go, but what worries me is the disappearance of King Arthur and his knights around the same time.

peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-the-gu.player: They haven't returned to their other realm have they?

peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-the-gu.speaker: Guard
peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-the-gu.text: No, there's no evidence to suggest that. It never sat well with the Sinclair children when their old man gave the castle to King Arthur and

peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-the-gu.speaker: Guard
peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-the-gu.text: moved the family to this mansion. I suspect the murder of old Sinclair was just the first step in a deeper plot to retake their 'birthright'.

peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-the-gu.player: How goes the investigation, then? What evidence have you gathered so far?

peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-the-gu.speaker: Guard
peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-the-gu.text: That's the problem. The Seers' Village council has forbidden the guards from breaking into Camelot or the Sinclair Mansion for further investigation.

peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-the-gu.speaker: Guard
peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-the-gu.text: They claim it's a breach of privacy or something like that. My suspicions mean nothing without proof to back them up, but I can't get proof without losing my job.

peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-the-gu.player: Which is why you're happy to see me, right? A rogue party could break into the mansion and investigate further, without the fear of losing their job. Am I right?

peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-the-gu.speaker: Guard
peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-the-gu.text: Exactly! I'm sure you'll manage to find a way into the house.

peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-pierre.player: Hi. I was wondering, do you know why the mansion is all locked up?

peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-pierre.speaker: Pierre
peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-pierre.text: I'm not meant to talk to anyone outside the family. On pain of death.

peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-pierre.player: That's a bit harsh. Thanks anyway.

peril-at-the-end-house-stanford-after-ta.speaker: Stanford
peril-at-the-end-house-stanford-after-ta.text: 'Allo, what can I do for you?

peril-at-the-end-house-stanford-after-ta.player: I'm trying to get into the mansion. Do you know why it's all locked up?

peril-at-the-end-house-stanford-after-ta.speaker: Stanford
peril-at-the-end-house-stanford-after-ta.text: I wasn't privy to the reason, but the whole family upped and left not long ago. Since then, I haven't heard a peep from anyone. I was told not to enter the mansion or to speak about their departure.

peril-at-the-end-house-stanford-after-ta.player: But you're willing to speak to me?

peril-at-the-end-house-stanford-after-ta.speaker: Stanford
peril-at-the-end-house-stanford-after-ta.text: Didn't say I was going to obey them, did I?

peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-gossip.speaker: Gossip
peril-at-the-end-house-talking-to-gossip.text: Soooooo? What did the guard have to say?

steps.player: The guard asked me to break into the Sinclair Mansion and search for clues about where they had gone.
He said...
that you were a gossip and I shouldn't divulge privileged information.

breaking-and-entering-talking-to-hobbes.speaker: Hobbes
breaking-and-entering-talking-to-hobbes.text: What are you doing here? I thought the house was locked up tight.

breaking-and-entering-talking-to-hobbes.player: Oh, it is, except for that broken window... Very convenient.
Where has the Sinclair family gone?

breaking-and-entering-talking-to-hobbes.speaker: Hobbes
breaking-and-entering-talking-to-hobbes.text: I'm under strict orders not to speak to anyone not of the Sinclair family.

breaking-and-entering-talking-to-hobbes.speaker: Hobbes
breaking-and-entering-talking-to-hobbes.text: I was told if I left the house that I would be killed!

breaking-and-entering-talking-to-hobbes.player: I think you need to look for a new job. Your employers are a bit scary.

breaking-and-entering-talking-to-louisa.speaker: Louisa
breaking-and-entering-talking-to-louisa.text: What are you doing in here? I didn't think anyone could enter or leave this place.

breaking-and-entering-talking-to-louisa.player: I'm looking for clues as to where the Sinclair family has gone. Why can't anyone enter or leave?

breaking-and-entering-talking-to-louisa.speaker: Louisa
breaking-and-entering-talking-to-louisa.text: We were told a curse had been placed on us. If we left the mansion we'd be struck down in an instant.

breaking-and-entering-talking-to-mary.speaker: Mary
breaking-and-entering-talking-to-mary.text: Who...? Oh, I remember you! You were asking all those questions about Lord Sinclair's murder. You had all sorts of evid-whats-its.

breaking-and-entering-talking-to-mary.player: Yes, that was me. Now I'm trying to find out where the Sinclair family has gone.

breaking-and-entering-talking-to-mary.speaker: Mary
breaking-and-entering-talking-to-mary.text: I don't know. They got really secretive after Lord Sinclair was killed and then suddenly left. That's all I know.

breaking-and-entering-talking-to-donovan.speaker: Donovan the Family Handyman
breaking-and-entering-talking-to-donovan.text: You aren't here to murder us in our sleep are you?

breaking-and-entering-talking-to-donovan.player: Well, I'd not be doing a very good job of it, if I was, considering you're not asleep.

breaking-and-entering-talking-to-donovan.speaker: Donovan the Family Handyman
breaking-and-entering-talking-to-donovan.text: So, you are here to kill us!

breaking-and-entering-searching-the-book.text: You find a piece of Black Knight armour, which seems very out of place in the Sinclair Mansion.
You've already searched this bookcase for clues.

breaking-and-entering-using-any-of-the-e.speaker: Mary/Donovan/Louisa/Hobbes/Pierre/Stanford
breaking-and-entering-using-any-of-the-e.text: I don't know anything about that.

breaking-and-entering-returning-to-the-g.speaker: Guard
breaking-and-entering-returning-to-the-g.text: Any luck getting into the mansion? Did you get some evidence?

options.text: I have proof that the Sinclairs have left.

steps.player: I have proof that the Sinclairs have left.

steps.text: File:Address form detail.png

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: A form? What does this prove?

steps.player: Don't you see? The Sinclairs have left for good. They premeditated their departure from the mansion.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Ah! Of course. Unfortunately, they filled in all of the form except where their new address is.
If the player has lost the scrap paper

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Really? Where?

steps.player: Errr, I seem to have left it somewhere.

options.text: I have proof that links the Sinclairs to Camelot.

steps.player: I have proof that links the Sinclairs to Camelot.

steps.text: You present the guard with the scrap of paper.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Aha! They've gone to the desert. They're meeting up with a camel.

steps.player: No...It's not camel, like the animal. The note isn't whole, they were writing the word Camelot. They were meeting at Camelot, this is our evidence to connect the Sinclairs to King Arthur.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Oh, right. Well, it connects them to King Arthur, but it doesn't prove that they had any bad intent towards him. For all we know they were going to a party.

options.text: I have proof of foul play.

steps.player: I have proof of foul play.

steps.text: You present the guard with the black full helm.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Hmm, this armour resembles Black Knight armour. The only Black Knights on this side of White Wolf Mountain are those that work for Morgan Le Faye.

steps.player: Exactly. And we know Morgan Le Faye has a history of harassing Merlin and King Arthur.
Since there is no sign of a struggle inside the Sinclair Mansion, we can only assume the knights were there by request.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Oh right! With this evidence and the note you brought me, we know they had intentions to do harm to King Arthur.
After showing all 3 pieces of evidence to the guard:

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Thank you, [player name]. We have all the proof we need to present to the Seers' Village council that something suspicious is going on.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: They'll review the evidence and hopefully give me permission to take a team to Camelot. It shouldn't be too difficult to get to the bottom of this.

steps.player: When do you expect to go to Camelot? Perhaps I could assist you?

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Oh the Seers' Village council convenes in a month or so, I'll present it then. No doubt they'll want a few days to review the evidence.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: We'll go sometime after that...if none of the other guards are on holiday. There are only four of us, ya know.

steps.player: WHAT?
A month or more? King Arthur could be in grave danger. Morgan Le Faye is involved and she is not one to be trifled with. One of the Sinclairs has already committed murder, who's to say another won't?
And you're going to wait a MONTH?

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: I have to follow procedure, my hands are tied.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: However, were a rogue adventurer to take the matter in to their own hands...

steps.player: Aye, what then?

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Well, if I were them, I would learn as much as I can about the Sinclair family history.

steps.player: That's all the advice you can give?

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Well, often the best historians are the town gossips. I'd start there. Good luck, brave adventurer!

steps.player: Never mind.

breaking-and-entering-talking-to-the-gua.player: What should I be doing again?

breaking-and-entering-talking-to-the-gua.speaker: Guard
breaking-and-entering-talking-to-the-gua.text: Find out all you can about the Sinclair family history. I'm sure there is a clue or two there.

snooping-around-asking-gossip-about-the-.player: Hello again. Can you tell me about the Sinclair family history?

snooping-around-asking-gossip-about-the-.speaker: Gossip
snooping-around-asking-gossip-about-the-.text: Hmph. I don't see why I should tell you anything.

snooping-around-asking-gossip-about-the-.speaker: Gossip
snooping-around-asking-gossip-about-the-.text: Perhaps if you had been less rude to me, I would have been willing to tell you.

snooping-around-asking-gossip-about-the-.player: I'm sorry I was rude. You are a vital part of this investigation. Unless you tell me about the Sinclairs, I won't be able to continue.

snooping-around-asking-gossip-about-the-.speaker: Gossip
snooping-around-asking-gossip-about-the-.text: Vital part, you say? So, I'll get credit for assistance? Well...I do know quite a bit about their history. I suppose I can't hold up an investigation as important as this. What do you want to know?

steps.player: Tell me about the family.

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: I've heard plenty about each of them...but I'll try to keep it as short as I can.

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: Old Lord Sinclair was a well respected man this side of White Wolf. He was great friends with King Ulthas and did many good works for the kingdom.

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: His children on the other hand were spoiled and horrid. They cared for no one but themselves and gave themselves such aires. Each had their own vice, but I didn't expect any of them would be driven to murder!

steps.player: What have they been up to since the arrest of their sibling?

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: They've been living very quietly, a nice change from the norm. But almost too quietly. I always thought they'd get into more trouble. No good will come from them, let me tell you!

steps.player: Tell me about the mansion.

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: The mansion? The mansion is quite new. Originally, the Sinclair family lived in Camelot, although it went under a different name then.

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: But when King Arthur and his knights appeared, old Lord Sinclair agreed with King Ulthas that the knights had greater need for the castle than the Sinclair family.

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: So, Lord Sinclair had the mansion built, packed his family up and vacated. His children were furious with him for doing it.

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: They felt themselves far better than the knights and felt insulted at having to live in a stuffy mansion.

steps.player: What happened next?

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: Well, you should know best... Anna killed her father. Poor man.

steps.player: Tell me about Anna Sinclair.

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: Anna? The guards are keeping her in the jail in the courthouse in Seers' Village. I hear she's been acting like a royal pain.

steps.player: But what is she like? Can she be reasoned with?

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: Reasoned with? She killed her own father!

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: I hear she's being so unreasonable that no lawyer in Gielinor will represent her. She's going to get a guilty verdict for sure.

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: Still, I go and visit her at the Seers' Village courthouse sometimes to try and keep her spirits up.

steps.player: Never mind.

snooping-around-talking-to-gossip-again.player: Could I ask you about the Sinclair family again?

snooping-around-talking-to-gossip-again.speaker: Gossip
snooping-around-talking-to-gossip-again.text: Well, I'm not one to gossip, but as it's for your investigation... What would you like to know?

snooping-around-talking-to-the-guard-aft.player: Where is Anna Sinclair being held?

snooping-around-pierre.player: What can you tell me about Anna Sinclair?

snooping-around-pierre.speaker: Pierre
snooping-around-pierre.text: What? I'm no gossip; I've got nothing to say about it.

snooping-around-stanford.player: What can you tell me about Anna?

snooping-around-stanford.speaker: Stanford
snooping-around-stanford.text: Why do you want to know about her?

snooping-around-stanford.player: I may need her help to get in touch with the rest of the Sinclairs.

snooping-around-stanford.speaker: Stanford
snooping-around-stanford.text: Good luck, mate. She's a right pain in the...

snooping-around-stanford.speaker: Stanford
snooping-around-stanford.text: Sorry, you still here? I started thinking about turnips.

snooping-around-hobbes.player: What can you tell me about Anna?

snooping-around-hobbes.speaker: Hobbes
snooping-around-hobbes.text: Anna? She was a spoiled brat, that's for sure.

snooping-around-hobbes.player: Can't you tell me anything more useful than that?

snooping-around-louisa.player: What can you tell me about Anna Sinclair?
Because she may be responsible for murder!

snooping-around-louisa.speaker: Louisa
snooping-around-louisa.text: Oh yes. Well, I can't say I ever liked Anna. She was always chasing after some boy or other.

snooping-around-mary.player: What can you tell me about Anna?

snooping-around-mary.speaker: Mary
snooping-around-mary.text: Anna? I don't know very much.

snooping-around-mary.player: You must have been privy to some of the children's secrets. Anything would be helpful.

snooping-around-mary.speaker: Mary
snooping-around-mary.text: No, I don't know anything like that. I kept my head down and did my work.

snooping-around-donovan.player: What can you tell me about Anna Sinclair?

snooping-around-donovan.speaker: Donovan the Family Handyman
snooping-around-donovan.text: Well, she's a murderer. What more could you need to know?

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-guard-1-at-t.speaker: Guard
devil-s-advocate-talking-to-guard-1-at-t.text: That Sinclair woman is such a pain! She keeps demanding gourmet meals and ridiculous things like silk sheets.

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-guard-1-at-t.speaker: Guard
devil-s-advocate-talking-to-guard-1-at-t.text: Go ahead. It means she won't be demanding things from me.

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-guard-2-at-t.speaker: Guard
devil-s-advocate-talking-to-guard-2-at-t.text: Mother said to join the guards, see the world! What do I end up doing? Guarding some stuck-up brat in a backwater village full of hippies.

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-guard-2-at-t.player: May I speak to the prisoner?

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna.speaker: Anna
devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna.text: Hmmm...yes, you were that nosy person asking all those questions about daddy's murder.

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna.player: So he's 'daddy' now is he? If he was so dear to you why did you kill him?

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna.speaker: Anna
devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna.text: I didn't! No one will believe me. It was my brother. He set me up.

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna.player: But there's hard evidence against you.

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna.speaker: Anna
devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna.text: It's forged! I swear, I never touched that dagger or poisoned my father.

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna.player: I didn't come here to just chit-chat. I need to know where your family has disappeared to. I have suspicions they've reclaimed Camelot.

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna.speaker: Anna
devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna.text: How should I know? I've been locked up here since you stuck your nose into our family's business.

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna.player: Well, I'll be off then. Have fun spending the rest of your life in jail.

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna.speaker: Anna
devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna.text: I... I might know how to find them...but I need a favour from you in return.

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna.speaker: Anna
devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna.text: I need a defence lawyer. None of the ones around here will represent me, they all think I'm guilty.

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna.player: Maybe it's because you ARE guilty. Your sibling offered hard proof you did it!

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna.speaker: Anna
devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna.text: No he didn't! He just said he saw me in the room. Why does everyone believe him?

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna.speaker: Anna
devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna.text: Can't you see he framed me? I was the scapegoat so they could all inherit their fortunes and live the good life.

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna.player: Why should I believe you? As far as I know you did kill your father.

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna.speaker: Anna
devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna.text: I don't care if you don't believe me. I know I'm innocent...but I'm also the only one that can show you how to get into Camelot. There's a secret passage that I discovered as a child when we lived there.

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna.player: So, if I agree to get you a 'not guilty' verdict at trial, you promise to tell me how to get into this secret passage that will lead me straight into Camelot?

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna.speaker: Anna
devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna.text: Yes! Exactly. So, what do you say?

options.text: Okay, I guess I don't have much of a choice.

steps.player: Okay, I guess I don't have much of a choice. I'll go start gathering evidence.

steps.speaker: Anna
steps.text: Try speaking to the servants at the Mansion. They'll probably be able to give you useful testimony.

steps.speaker: Anna
steps.text: Wait, take this.
She hands you a thread.

steps.speaker: Anna
steps.text: You can use it as evidence.

steps.player: Of what, your guilt?

steps.speaker: Anna
steps.text: No, show it to the servants. You'll find one of my siblings wears similar colours.

steps.player: No, thank you.

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna-after-a.player: I'm working on it. It's not exactly easy to unprove something that's true.

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna-after-a.speaker: Anna
devil-s-advocate-talking-to-anna-after-a.text: Try speaking to the servants at the Mansion. They'll probably be able to give you useful testimony.

devil-s-advocate-claiming-another-crimin.player: I need a piece of thread from the clothes you wore the night of the murder.
I might need to show it to people when I ask them questions about the murder. It's evidence in the case.

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-gossip-after.speaker: Gossip
devil-s-advocate-talking-to-gossip-after.text: I hear you're the defence lawyer for Anna, now.

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-gossip-after.player: How can you possibly know that already?

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-gossip-after.speaker: Gossip
devil-s-advocate-talking-to-gossip-after.text: I'm the town gossip, I'm supposed to know this stuff. Are you preparing for the trial?

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-gossip-after.player: Well, I'm going to talk to the servants and see if I can learn anything new from them...but other than that, I don't really know what I'm doing.

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-gossip-after.speaker: Gossip
devil-s-advocate-talking-to-gossip-after.text: Well, my father was in the guards and he attended many trials. As a defence lawyer you need to disprove any evidence presented by the prosecution. Disproving it gives reasonable doubt as to whether or not your

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-gossip-after.player: But how do I know what evidence will be presented?

devil-s-advocate-talking-to-gossip-after.speaker: Gossip

the-king-in-the-stone-talking-to-wizard-.text: You'll need King Arthur's most prized possession. That will unravel Morgan's spell. Then you'll need a piece of granite, the same rock Arthur was turned into.

the-king-in-the-stone-talking-to-wizard-.player: That's not so difficult. I already have the Holy Grail, King Arthur's most prized possession, and I know he was turned into a granite statue.

the-king-in-the-stone-talking-to-wizard-.speaker: Wizard Cromperty
the-king-in-the-stone-talking-to-wizard-.text: Let me just get that spell scroll for you...

steps.text: If the player already has an animate rock scroll

steps.speaker: Wizard Cromperty
steps.text: Oh, it looks like you still have the scroll I gave you.

the-king-in-the-stone-talking-to-wizard-.player: So what do I do with this spell?

the-king-in-the-stone-talking-to-wizard-.speaker: Wizard Cromperty
the-king-in-the-stone-talking-to-wizard-.text: Take the scroll, the Holy Grail and a piece of granite, any amount will do, to the statue of King Arthur. Once in front of him, read the scroll and the magic should do the rest.

the-king-in-the-stone-talking-to-wizard-.speaker: Wizard Cromperty
the-king-in-the-stone-talking-to-wizard-.text: Where is King Arthur being kept, anyway?

the-king-in-the-stone-talking-to-wizard-.player: Merlin suspects King Arthur had been taken to the Black Knights' Fortress. The last time I was there I needed to disguise myself in a bronze medium helm and an iron chainbody just to get past the door.

the-king-in-the-stone-talking-to-wizard-.speaker: Wizard Cromperty
the-king-in-the-stone-talking-to-wizard-.text: Well, that should still get you into the fortress, but I imagine you'll need a better disguise than that to reach King Arthur. He's a very important person and will be well guarded by the Black Knights.

the-king-in-the-stone-talking-to-wizard-.speaker: Wizard Cromperty
the-king-in-the-stone-talking-to-wizard-.text: Hmm...I wonder...if you used a magical object that turned you into stone on the statue, would it turn him back to being human? I must research that...

the-king-in-the-stone-talking-to-wizard-.speaker: Wizard Cromperty
the-king-in-the-stone-talking-to-wizard-.text: Oh, are you still here? Go on then, you've got a king to save!

the-king-in-the-stone-talking-to-wizard-.speaker: Wizard Cromperty
the-king-in-the-stone-talking-to-wizard-.text: Hello there. My name is Cromperty. I am a wizard, and an inventor.

the-king-in-the-stone-talking-to-wizard-.speaker: Wizard Cromperty
the-king-in-the-stone-talking-to-wizard-.text: You must be [player name]. My good friend Sedridor has told me about you. As both wizard and inventor, he has aided me in my great invention!

the-king-in-the-stone-talking-to-wizard-.speaker: Wizard Cromperty
the-king-in-the-stone-talking-to-wizard-.text: Why hello, [player name], what can I do for you?

options.text: What did I need for the spell to work?

steps.player: What did I need for the spell to work?

steps.speaker: Wizard Cromperty
steps.text: Take the scroll, the Holy Grail and a piece of granite, of any size, shape or weight, to the statue of King Arthur. Once in front of him, read the scroll and the magic should do the rest.

options.text: How do I get into the Black Knights' Fortress?

steps.player: How do I get into the Black Knights' Fortress?

steps.speaker: Wizard Cromperty
steps.text: How should I know, I'm just a simple wizard.

steps.speaker: Wizard Cromperty
steps.text: However, from what you said about having to wear a helm and chainmail, it sounds like you were disguised as a mere guard.

steps.player: And...

steps.speaker: Wizard Cromperty
steps.text: Well, King Arthur's statue wouldn't be trusted to mere guards. Only fully-fledged Black Knights will guard it. So you'll need to disguise yourself as one of them if you want to get access to the statue.

steps.player: Of course! Thanks, Wizard Cromperty.
Never mind.

infiltrating-the-black-knights-fortress-.speaker: Fortress Guard
infiltrating-the-black-knights-fortress-.text: I heard something happened to King Arthur and that Lord Daquarius was behind it.

infiltrating-the-black-knights-fortress-.player: Really? Where is King Arthur now?

infiltrating-the-black-knights-fortress-.speaker: Fortress Guard
infiltrating-the-black-knights-fortress-.text: I have no idea, but it's a great victory for Lord Daquarius. To take such a mighty supporter of the White Knights down... Truly brilliant.

infiltrating-the-black-knights-fortress-.speaker: Fortress Guard
infiltrating-the-black-knights-fortress-.text: Good day, brave knight. Congratulations on your victory against King Arthur.

infiltrating-the-black-knights-fortress-.player: Errr, thanks. Why don't you tell me in your own words how glorious you thought our victory was.

infiltrating-the-black-knights-fortress-.speaker: Fortress Guard
infiltrating-the-black-knights-fortress-.text: Of course. It was so clever of Lord Daquarius to lend our men to Morgan Le Faye in exchange for our prize. We got the better end of the deal, no doubt.

infiltrating-the-black-knights-fortress-.speaker: Guard
infiltrating-the-black-knights-fortress-.text: Hey, what are you doing? You can't go in there.

infiltrating-the-black-knights-fortress-.player: I don't have everything necessary to cast the spell.
I need to bring you some guard armour to disguise yourself in or you'll never be able to escape.

infiltrating-the-black-knights-fortress-.speaker: King Arthur
infiltrating-the-black-knights-fortress-.text: Very well. I'll await you here.

infiltrating-the-black-knights-fortress-.speaker: King Arthur
infiltrating-the-black-knights-fortress-.text: Thank you! I was afraid that would be the end of me.

infiltrating-the-black-knights-fortress-.player: It's no trouble. But we need to get you out of here quickly before any of the Black Knights suspect something.

infiltrating-the-black-knights-fortress-.speaker: King Arthur
infiltrating-the-black-knights-fortress-.text: The Black Knights? I thought Morgan did this to me.

infiltrating-the-black-knights-fortress-.player: There's no time to explain; here, take this disguise.

infiltrating-the-black-knights-fortress-.speaker: King Arthur
infiltrating-the-black-knights-fortress-.text: You leave first and I'll sneak out in a few minutes. Meet me back at Camelot and I shall reward you generously for your aid.

infiltrating-the-black-knights-fortress-.speaker: King Arthur
infiltrating-the-black-knights-fortress-.text: You leave first and I'll sneak out in a few minutes. Meet me back at Camelot and I shall reward you generously for your aid.

infiltrating-the-black-knights-fortress-.player: I should go meet King Arthur at Camelot. He should have escaped by now.

back-at-the-round-table-talking-to-king-.player: I see you made it back safely.

back-at-the-round-table-talking-to-king-.speaker: King Arthur
back-at-the-round-table-talking-to-king-.text: Indeed, thanks to the disguise you gave me. I arrived back just as Merlin had kicked out the Sinclair children. He scared them off with a few puffs of smoke and frogs. He told them if any of them left their house

back-at-the-round-table-talking-to-king-.speaker: King Arthur
back-at-the-round-table-talking-to-king-.text: again, he'd turn them all into rabbits.

back-at-the-round-table-talking-to-king-.player: I guess we won't be hearing a peep out of them for awhile.

back-at-the-round-table-talking-to-king-.speaker: King Arthur
back-at-the-round-table-talking-to-king-.text: Indeed. We of the Round Table are greatly indebted to you for all of your help. I wish to reward you for all the help you have given us...

back-at-the-round-table-talking-to-gossi.speaker: Gossip
back-at-the-round-table-talking-to-gossi.text: Do you have any interesting news?

back-at-the-round-table-talking-to-gossi.speaker: Gossip
back-at-the-round-table-talking-to-gossi.text: Then what are you standing around for!

back-at-the-round-table-talking-to-sincl.speaker: Guard
back-at-the-round-table-talking-to-sincl.text: I'm afraid I'm too busy to speak to you right now.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-king-arth.speaker: King Arthur
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-king-arth.text: Welcome, brave knight. I am always happy to see you back at my court. Please feel free to roam the castle and make use of the training grounds.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-king-arth.speaker: King Arthur
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-king-arth.text: My knights train daily on the top floor of Camelot. There they test their skills and strength against each other. Because of all the help you have given us, I open this training ground to you as well.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-king-arth.speaker: King Arthur
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-king-arth.text: Speak to the squire on the top floor of Camelot - he will explain the rules of the training grounds in detail.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-merlin.player: So how did you remove the Sinclairs from Camelot?

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-merlin.speaker: Merlin
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-merlin.text: Well, after I climbed out the vent, I snuck aboard a passing trade ship that dropped me at Catherby. From there, I returned to Camelot and used the Sinclairs own secret entrance against them. I used some of my

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-merlin.speaker: Merlin
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-merlin.text: own inventions to create a great deal of chaos and drove them from the house. Then I made sure they returned to their mansion and told them if they ever stepped foot from it again, I'd turn them all into rabbits.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-merlin.player: How did you get your magic powers back?

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-merlin.speaker: Merlin
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-merlin.text: Ah, Morgan's spell was not hard to break once I had access to my workshop. It's rather technical, so I won't bore you with the details.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-squire.speaker: Squire
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-squire.text: That door leads to the training ground for the Knights of the Round Table.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-squire.speaker: Squire
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-squire.text: Of course, my lord. But I must tell you the rules first. Would you like to hear them now?

steps.player: Yes please.

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: The training ground is a melee combat area only. Merlin has cast a spell over the grounds to prevent anyone using Prayer, Ranged or Magic.

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: Upon entering the grounds, you will fight each of the Round Table Knights in turn. Each knight is more skilled than the last, but all have different attack styles that can be exploited. There are eight knights in all, and

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: each will do damage not only to your hitpoints, but also your combat stats. If you should die in the grounds, Merlin will teleport you back here. You will not lose any of your items.

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: If you feel you cannot complete the battle, you may exit the training grounds. However, if you exit or die, you will have to start over with the first knight the next time you enter.

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: If you are a great warrior and defeat Sir Lancelot, mightiest of all knights, you will receive great rewards. Two new prayers will become available to you and your respawn point will be set to Camelot, as well as 20,000

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: XP in to each of your combat stats.

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: If you do not want your respawn set to Camelot, Merlin can change it for you.

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: Would you like me to repeat any of that for you?

steps.player: No, thank you.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-squire-ag.speaker: Squire
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-squire-ag.text: Good day, my lord. Is there anything I can do for you?

options.text: Tell me about the training ground.
Tell me about dying or leaving the grounds.

post-quest-dialogue-trying-to-enter-the-.text: Followers are not allowed in the Knight Waves. You'll need to put it away if you wish to enter.

post-quest-dialogue-upon-completing-the-.speaker: Merlin
post-quest-dialogue-upon-completing-the-.text: Well done, young adventurer. You truly are a worthy knight.
You receive access to the prayers Chivalry and Piety and 20,000 XP in your Hitpoints, Strength, Attack, and Defence skills. You may also speak to Merlin to set your respawn point to Camelot.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-merlin-ne.speaker: Merlin
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-merlin-ne.text: Excuse me for rushing off like this, but I must get back to my workroom.
